_help: CBSEMock 60-day reel campaign (weekdays, 1:01 PM IST). Ranked & fact-checked by Claude from the owner's plan, 19 Nov 2026. Writers turn each entry into campaign_reels/specs/NN-<slug>.py.

reels.hook: They cut marks even when your answer is right?
reels.brief: CBSE marking schemes give marks for correct steps, not only the final answer. Write the formula, substitution, working and unit — each step can earn marks.
reels.note: No '8–12 marks' or other number claims. Say 'can earn marks'.

reels.hook: Stop rereading. Start recalling.
reels.brief: Read 5 min → close the book → write everything you remember → check what you missed.
reels.cta: Save this and try it tonight
reels.note: Active recall; no exam claims.

reels.hook: Assertion–Reason in 10 seconds?
reels.brief: Test A alone, test R alone. Both true? Read 'A because R'. Makes sense → option A; else → B. One false → C or D.
reels.note: Must include a worked mini-example with a correct, verified answer. Use standard CBSE A–D option wording.

reels.topic: Where the marks are: Class 12 Maths
reels.hook: Class 12 Maths: where are the 80 marks?
reels.brief: Unit weightage 2026–27: Relations & Functions 8, Algebra 10, Calculus 35, Vectors & 3D 14, LP 5, Probability 8. Calculus is the biggest block — revise it first, but skip nothing.
reels.note: Verified: CBSE 2026–27 syllabus (Calculus 35/80). Recheck on cbseacademic.nic.in before writing.

reels.hook: One wrong sign can ruin a whole numerical.
reels.brief: Mirrors and lenses: write the sign convention (distances from pole/optical centre; along incident light +) and put signs on u, v, f BEFORE substituting.
reels.note: New Cartesian sign convention; check the example numbers in Python.

reels.hook: Your wrong answers are your best notes.
reels.brief: Wrong answer → why it was wrong → correct method. Review the notebook 10 minutes before each study session.

reels.hook: Before buying another guide, check these NCERT spots.
reels.brief: In-text questions, worked examples, activity conclusions and chapter-end exercises. Then NCERT Exemplar for practice.
reels.note: Do not say '90% of questions are NCERT' or 'lifted straight'. Say 'board papers follow the NCERT syllabus closely'.

reels.topic: Case study: read the question first
reels.hook: Case study? Read the questions before the passage.
reels.brief: Scan the questions first, then read the passage looking only for what they ask. Underline the data you need.

reels.hook: 3 marks? Write 3 clear points.
reels.brief: Examiners mark against value points in the marking scheme. Write distinct, numbered points instead of one long paragraph.
reels.note: Phrase as strategy, not a universal rule ('marking schemes list value points').

reels.hook: Your ray diagram is missing one tiny thing.
reels.brief: Every ray needs an arrow showing direction; real rays solid, virtual rays dotted; label F, 2F/C, object and image.
reels.note: Check the notes file for Light exists before linking; otherwise link mock papers.

reels.hook: Revise every chapter in 3 passes.
reels.brief: Pass 1 concepts → Pass 2 questions → Pass 3 only your mistakes.
reels.cta: Try it on your next chapter

reels.hook: A blank answer can only score zero.
reels.brief: Write what you know — the formula, a definition, the first steps or a labelled diagram. Partial answers can earn step marks.
reels.note: No '5 marks' claims.

reels.hook: Stuck on a numerical? Use G-F-S-U.
reels.brief: Given (in SI units) → Formula → Substitute → Unit in the answer. Show one quick worked example.
reels.note: Do NOT say '80% of marks before the calculation'. Compute the worked example in Python.

reels.hook: Make your answer easy to mark.
reels.brief: Use the key terms from the question and the NCERT keywords in your answer; underline them neatly (with a pencil or the same pen).
reels.note: Do not promise 'more generous marking'.

reels.hook: One page per chapter. Every formula.
reels.brief: Formula, what each symbol means, its unit and one example. Update as you practise.

reels.topic: Presentation that is easy to mark
reels.hook: Same answer. Which one is easier to mark?
reels.brief: Side-by-side: wall of text vs headings, points, spacing, a labelled diagram and boxed final answer.
reels.note: No 'extra marks' numbers.

reels.hook: Turn every heading into a question.
reels.brief: Heading → question → answer from memory → check the book.

reels.hook: 3 questions. 3 seconds each.
reels.brief: Three quick Class 10 Science MCQs (2026–27 syllabus), countdown, reveal each answer with a one-line reason.
reels.note: Every answer verified; exactly one correct option each.

reels.hook: Planning to pass on grace marks?
reels.brief: There is no automatic 5–10 mark bonus for everyone. Results follow CBSE's evaluation and moderation policy — plan to earn every mark with steps and attempts.
reels.note: Don't state specific moderation numbers. Neutral, factual.

reels.hook: Diagram questions: draw first, then explain.
reels.brief: When a question asks for a diagram: neat pencil drawing, labels with straight leader lines, a title — then the explanation.
reels.note: Don't claim fixed marks per diagram.

reels.hook: 25 minutes on. 5 minutes off.
reels.brief: Focus 25 min on one task, 5-min break away from the phone, repeat 4 times then a longer break.

reels.hook: One revision is not enough.
reels.brief: Revise the same day, next day, after 3 days and after 7 days. Solve one question each time.

reels.hook: Name the SI unit before time runs out.
reels.brief: 3 quick quantities (e.g., resistivity, electric potential, power of a lens) with 4 unit options, countdown, reveal.
reels.note: Verify units; keep quantities in 2026–27 syllabus.

reels.hook: Answered both choices? Here's what CBSE counts.
reels.brief: CBSE's June 2026 clarification: when you attempt more than required (e.g., both internal choices), only the best-scoring attempt is counted. But extra answers cost time — choose one and write it well.
reels.note: Source: CBSE circular CBSE/COORD/TOTALING/CLASS XII/2026 (June 2026). Re-verify before writing; say 'as per CBSE's 2026 clarification'.

reels.hook: Guess the answer before you calculate.
reels.brief: Estimate the size/range first, then calculate; if the result is far off, check units and powers of ten.
reels.note: Worked example computed in Python.

reels.hook: Can you teach it in 30 seconds?
reels.brief: Explain the topic aloud without notes as if to a younger student; where you get stuck is what to revise.

reels.hook: Your revision plan is too vague.
reels.brief: Each day: 3 subjects — one weak topic, one practice set, one recall session. Write it for the week.

reels.hook: 3 seconds per question — ready?
reels.brief: Three quick Class 10/12 Chemistry MCQs (2026–27 syllabus), countdown, reveal with reason.
reels.note: Verify every answer; balance any equation.

reels.hook: PYQs won't tell you the exact questions.
reels.brief: Use PYQs to learn formats and common question styles: sort by concept, solve without looking, note what each tested.
reels.note: Never imply a question will repeat.

reels.hook: Long answers can hide the point.
reels.brief: A rambling 2-mark answer vs two precise points with the key terms.

reels.hook: Behind schedule? Don't plan 12-hour days.
reels.brief: List pending chapters, start with prerequisites and manageable high-weightage topics, short daily blocks, keep one practice slot.
reels.note: Avoid fear language.

reels.hook: 3 hours. How should you split them?
reels.brief: Example plan: reading time to choose OR options and plan → MCQs first at a steady pace → short answers → long answers → last 10–15 minutes to check. Practise your own split in a timed mock.
reels.note: Present as a sample plan, not an official rule; papers differ by subject.

reels.hook: Map questions: locate, label, check spelling.
reels.brief: Quick map challenge: mark the place, write the name neatly, use the symbol/legend asked. Countdown + reveal.
reels.note: Use only map items from the 2026–27 Class 10 SST map list.

reels.hook: Use reading time to decide, not just read.
reels.brief: Question paper is given 15 minutes before writing starts. You can't write answers then — read the whole paper, choose your OR options, plan the order and recall formulas.
reels.note: No '+15 marks' or 'lock in 20 marks'. Students may not write on the question paper during reading time.

reels.hook: A correct number without a unit is incomplete.
reels.brief: Show an answer with no unit, then the fixed answer with the unit and a quick unit check.
reels.note: Example computed in Python.

reels.hook: Don't just check your score.
reels.brief: Sort mistakes: concept, recall, time, careless. Pick one fix for each before the next paper.

reels.hook: Only 30 minutes? Use this reset.
reels.brief: 5 min headings → 10 min recall → 10 min questions → 5 min error review.

reels.hook: Which keyword makes this answer precise?
reels.brief: Vague statement + 3 keyword options; reveal the most precise term with one line of context (Class 10/12 Biology, 2026–27 syllabus).
reels.note: Verify biology facts.

reels.topic: How many mock papers before boards?
reels.hook: How many full papers should you solve?
reels.brief: Quality over count: full timed papers under exam conditions, same-day error review, then re-practise weak topics. Aim for a steady weekly routine.
reels.note: Don't promise outcomes. Mock Zone papers should be repeat-free by then — check mockzone status.

reels.hook: Explain, state, compare — not the same task.
reels.brief: State = short fact; Explain = reason/how; Compare = both sides point by point; Justify = give evidence. Mini example for each.

reels.hook: Busy day? Protect 20 minutes.
reels.brief: 10 min recall + 5 min wrong answers + 5 min one timed question.

reels.hook: Last 30 minutes: finish, check, correct.
reels.brief: Don't start a brand-new long answer in panic; complete unfinished answers, check calculations, units, question numbers and diagrams.
reels.note: Strategy, not a rule.

reels.hook: One bad mock is data, not your result.
reels.brief: Review 3 errors, redo them without the solution, schedule a retest in 3 days.
reels.note: Encouraging tone.
